title: Feedback Delta Scanner & Probe Ledger
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight synthesis of customer feedback collected between 2026-08-15 and 2026-09-25 across NPS follow-ups, CSM interviews, support tickets, and field notes. The goal is to: 1) surface delta changes vs. previous quarter (what’s new), 2) compile concrete asks into probeable hypotheses, and 3) prioritize a set of quick experiments + engineering tickets that unblock high-impact customers.

Quick summary (tl;dr):
- New and recurring top asks: clearer cost attribution per-route/model, more predictable Dedicated autoscaling (burst behavior), and KV/prefix cache visibility for debugging.
- Emerging theme: customers want observability tied to user-facing metrics (conversations dropped, tail latency percentiles by customer) not just token counts.
- Quick wins (low effort): add a labeled sample of per-request cost breakdown to the Console call-detail view; create a short KB article showing how to interpret Dedicated burst logs.

Evidence highlights (selected snippets):
- "We had a client drop because their call costs jumped 3x overnight — we couldn't explain why." — Enterprise security fintech, Aug 2026
- "Can we pin the model to a quantized variant for cost reasons but still get the same output? Not sure how to test meaingfully." — mid-market consumer SaaS, support thread CS-4127
- "When a canary fails, we need a per-customer rollback hook. Right now fallback to hosted is opaque." — platform team at a marketplace, CSM interview 2026-09-12

Delta vs. prior synthesis (what’s shifted):
- Cost transparency rose from a low-velocity curiosity to urgent procurement blocker for several enterprise deals this quarter.
- Previously: customers accepted fuzzy autoscaling tradeoffs. Now: predictable burst capacity and contractual guarantees are becoming gating items.
- Debug visibility: customers want to tie KV-cache hits/misses to user-reported degradations (i.e., correlate prefix cache misses with high tail latency).

Consolidated asks (phrased as customer language, grouped):
1) Cost & billing clarity
   - "Show me per-route, per-model token + compute cost for the last 30 days (by user or API key)."
   - "Alert me when cost velocity spikes versus baseline for a given route."
2) Predictable Dedicated behavior
   - "We need a contractable burst SLA and a simple knob to reserve X% burst capacity for top routes."
   - "Explain how autoscaler decisions are made and expose the decision timeline."
3) Observability & debugging for cache/batching
   - "Why did our requests go from 200ms to 1.8s? Give me KV cache hit-rate + batch sizes per minute."
   - "Expose first-party traces that map request -> runtime variant (quantized/fp16) used."
4) Rollouts & failover control
   - "Canaries need to be able to shunt traffic back to previous model instantly per customer id."
   - "We want canary metrics surfaced in our dashboards (A/B per-customer cohorts)."
5) Private deployment security and onboarding friction
   - "KMS/HSM integration guide with example terraform modules."
   - "A checklist for air-gapped install (network ports, certs, firewall rules)."

Initial impact assessment (rough):
- Revenue blockers: cost transparency (high) — multiple procurement stalls.
- Retention risk: unpredictable Dedicated burst behavior (medium-high) for customers with heavy peak loads.
- Support load: KV/cache/debug gaps (medium) — leads to lengthy triage calls.

Probe ideas (experiments we can run quickly)
- Probe 1: Per-request cost sample card (2-week experiment)
  - Deliverable: add a small UI card in Console for a route showing token breakdown + compute estimate for a selected week.
  - Success metric: reduce "explain-my-bill" tickets by 30% on routes with card enabled.
  - Owner: Product Console (Priya) + CS wants 2 pilot customers.
- Probe 2: Dedicated burst-stubbing demo (4-week PoC)
  - Deliverable: a simulated burst policy toggle in staging that reserves X% capacity per route plus a synthetic load-runbook.
  - Success metric: 2 engaged customers sign a 3-month Dedicated trial.
  - Owner: Solutions Eng + Infra (Ethan).
- Probe 3: KV-cache diagnostics overlay (3-week)
  - Deliverable: store and surface cache hit-rate/eviction events in the call trace UI for last 24h, with simple correlation visual (latency vs hit-rate).
  - Success metric: support time-to-resolution for cache-related incidents drops by 40%.
  - Owner: Serving runtime + Observability (Lucas).

Priority backlog snapshot (p0/p1/p2)
- P0 (customer-blocking): per-route cost alerts + billing explanation card; contract language and design for Dedicated burst SLA.
- P1 (high ROI): KV-cache diagnostics overlay; per-customer canary rollback hook design.
- P2 (nice-to-have): KMS HSM terraform templates; enhanced cohort metrics in rollouts.

Suggested next steps (immediate owner + timing)
1) CS team to run two rapid customer validation calls (15–20 min) with customers flagged as high pain (list below) — due 2026-10-07. Owner: Maya
2) Product & Console: scope UI card and create a mockup — due 2026-10-11. Owner: Priya
3) Infra & Solutions: run the Dedicated burst-stubbing demo in staging and invite 1 pilot customer — demo week 2026-10-18. Owner: Ethan
4) Eng: quick feasibility review for KV-cache trace overlay; cost estimate (2 weeks) — due 2026-10-14. Owner: Lucas

Open questions and risks (notes-to-self style):
- How much of per-request compute cost can be estimated deterministically vs. modeled? (need Eng input).
- Legal: will contractable burst SLA require new indemnities or penalty clauses? Loop in legal early.
- Data privacy: exposing per-api-key cost by user may reveal usage patterns; check compliance and customer consent.

Customer candidates for validation calls (CS flagged):
- Fintech: AcornPay (high revenue, escalated billing spike Aug) — contact: N. Rivera (acct exec)
- Marketplace: Lendspace platform (needs canary rollback per customer) — contact: S. Wu (platform lead)
- SaaS: ComposeAI (interested in KV-cache insights) — contact: R. Singh (CTO)

Notes, raw fragments pulled from threads (unedited):
- "We had a batch of calls that were fine for a month and then bam — the next day calls doubled in token cost. No idea why, support asked for logs that were meaningless for us."
- "Our compliance team will not sign until KMS docs for private are in hand."
- "Can you show us how quantization changed output fidelity? We need examples and a rollback plan."

Action items (short checklist):
- [ ] Schedule 2 validation calls (Maya)
- [ ] Product mock for cost card (Priya)
- [ ] Feasibility notes for KV overlay (Lucas)
